---
title: "Data protection and security"
---

> **This page is a stub.** It describes what usRds does with your data today
> and the habits that keep USRDS files safe. It will grow as the package adds
> its own data-safety checks (see
> [issue #49](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/usRds/issues/49)).

USRDS files are patient-level records released under a data use agreement
(DUA). Your DUA is the rule that applies. This page does not replace it, and
nothing in usRds makes an analysis compliant on its own. If this page and your
DUA disagree, follow your DUA.

## What usRds does with your files today

- **It reads only the folder you name.** `set_USRDS_wd()` records the folder
  in the environment variable `USRDS_WD` and maps the files in it by name.
  When `USRDS_WD` is already set, loading the package maps the same folder
  again. Mapping reads file names only, not file contents.
- **It sends nothing anywhere.** usRds makes no network connections and
  uploads nothing. Your data stays on the machine where you run R.
- **It writes only where you tell it to.**
  - `convert_usrds_to_parquet()` writes Parquet files to the `target_dir` you
    give it, and nowhere else.
  - `set_USRDS_wd(permanent = TRUE)` adds one line to your `~/.Renviron` file:
    the folder path, not any data. With the default `permanent = FALSE`,
    nothing is written.
- **Results live in your R session.** Data frames returned by the `get_*()`
  and cohort functions are patient-level. They stay in memory until you save
  them somewhere.

## Habits that keep data safe

### Treat every copy as USRDS data

Parquet files made by `convert_usrds_to_parquet()`, extracts you save as
`.rds`, `.csv` or `.parquet`, and cohort data frames are all covered by your
DUA, just like the original SAS and CSV files. Keep them inside the approved
storage location your DUA names.

### Keep data out of code repositories

Keep the USRDS folder outside any git repository, and point usRds at it with
`set_USRDS_wd()` instead of copying files into your project. If data files do
have to sit inside a project folder, add ignore rules before the first commit,
for example:

```
# .gitignore: never commit data
*.sas7bdat
*.parquet
*.csv
*.rds
*.RData
*.rda
```

Adapt the list to your project: a rule such as `*.csv` also ignores public
CSV files you may want to commit. A file committed once stays in the
repository's history even after you delete it, so check `git status` before
each commit.

### Do not save the workspace

An `.RData` file saved when R closes can hold every patient-level data frame
from the session. In RStudio, set *Tools > Global Options > General >
Save workspace to .RData on exit* to **Never**, and turn off *Restore .RData
into workspace at startup*. `.Rhistory` can also hold values you printed.

### Keep paths out of shared code

Call `set_USRDS_wd()` once (or with `permanent = TRUE`) rather than writing
your data path into scripts you share. A path can reveal where restricted
data is stored, and it breaks the script on anyone else's machine.

### Check small cells before sharing results

Tables, figures and model output can identify people when counts are small.
The CMS cell size suppression policy, which applies to Medicare data, does not
allow cells of 1 to 10 to be shown, or values from which such a cell could be
worked out. Check the rule in your own DUA before you share any output.

### Be careful with web tools and AI assistants

Do not paste rows, upload files, or share screenshots of USRDS data with web
services, including AI coding assistants, unless your DUA allows it. Sharing
code, error messages with values removed, and made-up example data is a safer
way to get help.

## Planned protections

The plan in [issue #49](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/usRds/issues/49)
adds checks to the package itself. Names are provisional and none of these
exist yet:

- a read-only data-safety check when the package is attached, which notes
  missing protections in a git repository and warns (by path only) about
  data-like files that would be committed; turn it off with
  `options(usRds.safety_check = FALSE)`;
- the same check in `set_USRDS_wd()` and `convert_usrds_to_parquet()`;
- `check_repo_for_usrds_data()`, which scans a folder for files that look
  like USRDS data;
- opt-in helpers to add ignore rules and a pre-commit check to a project;
- `check_small_cells()`, which reports cells below a threshold (fewer than
  11 by default) in data frames, tables, plots and survival fits, without
  changing them.

This page will be updated as each one is added.
